headline: High risk: Langflow’s unsandboxed server-side flows can ingest Kotaemon outputs and files, creating default-path leakage, prompt injection, and cascading action errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kotaemon can ingest documents, PDFs, HTML, MHTML, DOCX, and chat transcripts, while Langflow chains tools and agents in graph-based flows and can read uploaded files from the server filesystem. That creates a plausible default path where Kotaemon-generated content is treated as trusted input by Langflow. The interaction is documented enough to avoid low, but not enough for high.
conditions: IF Langflow flow nodes consume Kotaemon-generated text or files without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF Kotaemon outputs are copied into Langflow prompts or file inputs, attacker-controlled instructions can traverse the pair.
mitigations: Add a provenance banner to all Kotaemon exports before import into Langflow.
Disable automatic prompt concatenation in Langflow flows.
Require a manual review step for any HTML/MHTML/DOCX ingested from Kotaemon.
Use separate workspaces for the two agents.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the handoff boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kotaemon touches API keys and chat transcripts and writes to ./ktem_app_data, while Langflow reads and writes server filesystem data and stores per-flow credentials. Because both have broad network egress and file access, a shared deployment or handoff can expose sensitive documents or secrets in default configurations. The blast radius is multiple work products and credentials, not just one file.
conditions: IF both agents are deployed on the same host or shared volume, file contents can cross between them.
IF Kotaemon outputs API keys or transcripts into files that Langflow reads, leakage occurs.
IF Langflow flows send uploaded content to external model providers, sensitive data can leave the boundary.
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate container and volume.
Rotate any API keys already handled by Kotaemon.
Restrict Langflow flows from reading Kotaemon data directories.
Disable external model providers for sensitive flows.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage ACLs and egress allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Kotaemon can support multiple instances and uses a local data directory, while Langflow has server-side filesystem write, shell execution, subprocess spawning, package installation, and shared server-side state. If both run on the same deployment or workspace, they can concurrently mutate overlapping files or resources without locking, making destructive conflicts plausible by default and potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF both agents share a writable directory, concurrent writes can corrupt state.
IF Langflow flows install packages or spawn subprocesses against the same environment Kotaemon uses, environment drift can break either agent.
IF both instances run simultaneously without external locking, race conditions can overwrite outputs.
mitigations: Run each agent in its own container.
Mount separate writable directories.
Disable package installation in Langflow for shared hosts.
Schedule non-overlapping maintenance windows.
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional storage for shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow is explicitly a graph-based flow builder that can chain multiple agents and tools, so Kotaemon outputs can become Langflow inputs with little inherent verification. Kotaemon produces citations and chat transcripts, which Langflow may render or act on as authoritative flow inputs. That makes downstream mistakes or fabricated content likely to cascade into actions or reports.
conditions: IF Langflow uses Kotaemon output as a prompt or tool input without validation, errors propagate.
IF a Langflow flow triggers external APIs based on Kotaemon-generated facts, incorrect actions can occur.
IF citations from Kotaemon are rendered without checking source integrity, false attribution can spread.
mitigations: Insert a verification step between Kotaemon and Langflow.
Require source-link checks before any action-taking node.
Mark Kotaemon output as untrusted in Langflow prompts.
Limit Langflow flows to read-only analysis for this handoff.
requires-engineering: add schema validation and citation verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Kotaemon handles chat transcripts, documents, and API keys, while Langflow stores per-flow credentials and processes uploaded files on a server filesystem. The pair therefore creates a compliance mismatch risk around retention and subject-rights handling even without a specific residency claim. I do not cite only one agent because the risk arises from their combined handling and storage patterns.
conditions: IF regulated documents or transcripts are routed through both agents, retention obligations apply to both stores.
IF Langflow retains uploaded files longer than Kotaemon's local data policy, deletion requests may fail end-to-end.
IF either agent logs secrets or transcripts beyond the intended retention window, compliance gaps appear.
mitigations: Define a shared retention policy for both agents.
Exclude secrets from Langflow uploads.
Document deletion/export procedures for both stores.
Purge stale flow artifacts weekly.
requires-engineering: implement automated retention and deletion propagation.
